latest_justification.justification_narrative:
Patient John Doe (PT-88391) is evaluated by Dr. Aris Thorne, MD, for severe right knee osteoarthritis (ICD-10: M17.11), and is requesting authorization for Total Knee Arthroplasty (CPT 27447) under Aetna Health policy POL-AETNA-2026-KNEE. The patient presents with a symptom duration of 14 months, reporting constant pain rated 8/10 that severely impairs activities of daily living, specifically limiting walking to less than 50 feet, thereby fully satisfying CRIT-1.

Radiographic evidence from weight-bearing X-rays demonstrates severe medial joint space obliteration consistent with Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 osteoarthritis, meeting the requirements of CRIT-2. Furthermore, the patient has successfully completed and failed an exhaustive course of non-operative conservative therapy exceeding 12 weeks, which included 14 weeks of structured physical therapy, daily use of Meloxicam, and two triamcinolone intra-articular joint injections, satisfying CRIT-3.

Finally, the patient's Body Mass Index (BMI) is documented at 26.5 kg/m², which is well below the maximum threshold of 40.0 kg/m² mandated by CRIT-4. Given the complete alignment of clinical findings, imaging, and conservative treatment history with all payer policy criteria, Total Knee Arthroplasty is medically necessary to restore functional mobility and alleviate chronic pain.

latest_justification.justification_narrative:
Patient Jane Smith (PT-44209) is evaluated by Dr. Elena Rostova, MD, for lumbar radiculopathy (ICD-10: M54.16), presenting with L5-S1 left leg radicular pain and a pain score of 6/10. Physical examination reveals objective neurological deficits satisfying CRIT-3, specifically mild sensory loss along the L5 dermatome, 4+/5 left dorsiflexion strength, and a positive straight leg raise test at 45 degrees.

However, under policy POL-BCBS-2026-MRI-LUMBAR, the current documentation does not fully meet all mandatory coverage criteria. The patient's symptom duration is documented at 5 weeks, falling short of the required > 6 weeks duration for CRIT-1. Additionally, the patient has completed 4 weeks of outpatient physical therapy and a 10-day course of oral Methylprednisolone, which fails to satisfy the minimum 6-week conservative management requirement under CRIT-2.

Given the presence of objective motor weakness (4+/5 left dorsiflexion) and sensory loss along the L5 dermatome, expedited imaging may become medically necessary if symptoms persist or if progressive neurological deficits develop. At this juncture, the case requires either additional duration of conservative management to meet policy thresholds or a peer-to-peer review highlighting acute neurological compromise to request an exception.

latest_appeal.appeal_letter_narrative:
Dear Medical Director, We are submitting this formal appeal on behalf of our patient, Sarah Connor (PT-60481), to overturn the recent denial of a Lumbar Spine MRI without contrast (CPT 72148, ICD-10 M54.5). The initial adverse determination cited failure to meet Policy POL-BCBS-2026-MRI-LUMBAR Criterion CRIT-2 due to an absence of verified 6-week physical therapy attendance logs and physician progress notes confirming conservative treatment failure. We are writing to formally rebut this rationale with newly attached clinical documentation establishing clear fulfillment of all conservative care prerequisites.

Contrary to the prior determination, the patient has completed a rigorous, supervised course of conservative management. Specifically, the attached Physical Therapy Completion Log documents 12 completed sessions of structured physical therapy between June 1 and July 20, spanning a total duration of 7 weeks. Despite this dedicated 7-week therapeutic regimen, the patient experienced zero symptomatic relief, exhibiting persistent lower back pain and progressive left leg numbness lasting 10 weeks total. Physician progress notes from the Spine Clinic corroborate the complete failure of these conservative measures to mitigate the underlying pathology.

Given the persistence of radicular symptoms and neurological compromise (left leg numbness) lasting beyond six weeks despite documented physical therapy failure, advanced diagnostic imaging is clinically indicated to rule out structural nerve root compression, disc herniation, or other spinal pathology. Delaying imaging exposes the patient to the risk of permanent neurological deficit. We request an immediate reversal of this denial and prompt authorization for the requested lumbar spine MRI.
key_rebuttal_points: Patient completed 12 supervised physical therapy sessions over a 7-week duration, satisfying the 6-week conservative treatment threshold under Criterion CRIT-2.
Attached physical therapy completion logs and physician progress notes verify total conservative treatment failure with no symptomatic relief.
